    Constrained Buy-and-Hold Baseline (Executed, Full Metric Suite) Implementation Plan

    Overview: Implements a constrained buy-and-hold baseline that runs as a real backtest session (constant LONG, full equity, same RiskManager and full metric suite) for apples-to-apples comparison on every metric axis. Core changes: exit_enabled flags on stop-loss / take-profit (gate the exit action while keeping the level computed for sizing), a non-trainable always_long model, and experiment wiring. The field defaults to True, so historical configs keep their exact behavior with no backfill; an audit records that they are implicitly exit_enabled=true.

    Status: COMPLETE (2026-06-20) — all tasks done and verified end-to-end with a real ×3 run.

    For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

    Created: 2026-06-08

    Status: COMPLETE (2026-06-20). All seven tasks done; the constrained buy-and-hold baseline runs as a real backtest with the full investor metric suite and alpha_risk_constrained ≈ 0 under the ×3 RC-matched profile (D2/D3 flipped to the RC alternative). See per-task status notes below.

    Goal: Add a constrained buy-and-hold baseline that runs as a real backtest session through the existing engine, so it produces the FULL investor/execution metric suite (drawdown, Sortino, Calmar, exposure, costs, operational gates) under the same operational restrictions as the bot — enabling true apples-to-apples comparison on every metric axis, not just return/alpha.

    Architecture: Reuse the existing prediction seam and the uniformly-applied RiskManager. A buy-and-hold is just a decision policy that emits LONG. Two minimal, decoupled changes make it a pure buy-and-hold: (1) a always_long non-trainable baseline model that emits LONG; (2) a config flag exit_enabled on StopLossConfig/TakeProfitConfig that, when false, stops the bot from closing on SL/TP hits without changing how SL/TP are computed or used for sizing. All other exits are already disablable via existing config (exit_threshold=0.0, trailing_stop.enabled=false, risk-halt thresholds None). The buy-and-hold bot profile is attached only to its own experiment via the existing per-experiment bot_config override seam — no other experiment config is touched.

    Tech Stack: Python 3 / Pydantic v2 config models, PyTorch baseline-model interface, the Rainbow backtesting engine and bot-logic modules, the Script 2 experiment generator.

    0. Why This Design (Evidence Summary)

    These are the verified facts this plan relies on. Each is load-bearing.

    • The prediction seam is model-agnostic. engine_loop.py:525-541 consumes only prediction["signal"] (LONG/SHORT/NONE). Any decision policy plugs in here.
    • The RiskManager is applied uniformly to every backtest, built once from experiment_config.bot_config.risk_manager_config regardless of model type (runtime_context.py:166-171). So a baseline run inherits all operational constraints and the full metric pipeline for free.
    • There are exactly 5 exit causes in bot_logic.py generate_exit_orders:192-441 plus risk force-flat in engine_loop.py:564-590: stop-loss, take-profit, signal-flip, uncertainty exit, risk force-flat.
    • 4 of 5 exits are already disablable via existing config:
    • Signal-flip: never fires for an always-LONG policy (never emits the opposite signal).
    • Uncertainty exit: strategy_config.exit_threshold = 0.0 (bot_config.py:325).
    • Trailing stop: trailing_stop_config.enabled = false (bot_config.py:60).
    • Risk force-flat: max_drawdown_percent_stop = None, max_daily_loss = None, or force_flat_on_stop = false (bot_config.py:423).
    • Only SL/TP cannot be disabled today. StopLossConfig.type/TakeProfitConfig.type are Literal with no "none" option and value is required (bot_config.py:27,45); generate_entry_signals always computes an SL/TP price (bot_logic.py:550-612).
    • The SL/TP exit checks already guard on is not None (bot_logic.py:202,228,256,283), so gating them with a config flag is a localized change to the exit path only.
    • Position sizing decoupling: method="fixed" does NOT use the stop-loss distance (position_sizing.py:127-130); only method="risk_based" does (position_sizing.py:131-135). Because this plan keeps SL/TP computed (only the exit action is gated), sizing logic is identical for all runs — no method restriction, no divergent code path.
    • Config is default-tolerant, not strict. BaseConfig uses Pydantic extra="ignore"; missing keys resolve from DEFAULTS < bot.yaml < JSON < kwargs (base_config.py). This means an old snapshot missing exit_enabled still LOADS (defaults to True) — behaviorally identical to history — so leaving it as-is (no backfill) is safe; the snapshot is merely implicit rather than explicit about the field.
    • Resolved snapshots DO embed the full bot_config. Verified: data/plans/experiments/*/experiment_*.json and per-trial experiment_config.json embed strategy_config.stop_loss_config = {type, value} / take_profit_config = {type, value}. ~6,797 JSON files under data/ contain stop_loss_config (out of ~12,636 experiment JSONs). A blanket backfill would therefore touch thousands of files — which the no-backfill decision (D6) avoids: they load the True default instead.
    • The config also lives in the DB. experiments.experiment_config_json (models.py:144) and backtest_sessions.bot_config_json (models.py:458) store the resolved bot_config including stop_loss/take_profit. Under the no-backfill decision (D6) these are left as-is and load the exit_enabled=true default.
    • Two independent flags (confirmed): exit_enabled on StopLossConfig AND a separate exit_enabled on TakeProfitConfig, so SL and TP exits can be disabled independently.
    • No-backfill decision (Manu, 2026-06-19 — supersedes the 2026-06-08 completeness policy): historical JSON snapshots and DB config JSON are left as-is. Because the field defaults to True, they load as exit_enabled=true — exactly their historical behavior — so no rewrite is needed, and a blanket backfill would only churn config hashes for zero behavioral gain (the same lesson as the trailing-stop work). New snapshots get the key automatically (resolution merges bot.yaml); only a config that deliberately disables exits (the buy-and-hold profile) carries the key explicitly. An audit (Task 7) records that all historical configs are implicitly exit_enabled=true.
    • Templates are default-driven. A template legitimately loads with the bot.yaml default (exit_enabled=true), so nothing needs to be written into it. A template carries the key only when it deliberately overrides the default — e.g., the buy-and-hold profile in Task 5 sets exit_enabled: false.
    • A clean per-experiment bot_config override seam exists via experiment_defaults.bot_config + _deep_merge() in the Script 2 generator, so the buy-and-hold profile attaches only to its experiment.

    1. Critical Correctness Constraints

    These are non-negotiable and must hold throughout implementation:

    1. exit_enabled default MUST be True. A default of False would silently disable SL/TP exits for every existing experiment and every live-trading run. Default True preserves current behavior exactly.
    2. The flag gates the EXIT action only. generate_entry_signals still computes and stores SL/TP on the position; risk_based sizing still consumes the SL distance. The only behavioral change is in generate_exit_orders.
    3. bot-logic is shared with live trading. The change must be behavior-preserving when exit_enabled=True. No live profile may set it False unintentionally.
    4. No suppression, no legacy shims. No type: ignore, no _old aliases, no compatibility wrappers (project rules §3, §15).

    2. Open Decisions (recommended defaults; flip before execution)

    These are marked so Manu can override. The plan is written assuming the recommended option.

    # Decision Recommended Alternative
    D1 Decision policy implementation Dedicated always_long baseline model (clean cross-fold identity) Reuse rule_based with default_signal: "LONG" (zero new Python, but muddier report identity)
    D2 Position count Single full-capital position (max_concurrent_positions=1): "deploy capital once, hold" Fill N slots at t0 to mirror the synthetic Benchmark RC slot model (requires same_direction_cooldown_ticks=0, require_higher_confidence=false)
    D3 Capital deployment Near-full via position_sizing_method="fixed" with risk_per_trade + max_position_value_pct tuned to deploy ~100% of equity Match Benchmark RC sizing exactly
    D4 Sequencing vs investor-metrics Run after the investor-metrics engine instrumentation is live, so BH runs get the suite natively (live since 2026-06-10) Run now regardless
    D5 Short side Out of scope (buy-and-hold only) Add a sell_and_hold variant later
    D6 Existing snapshots/DB DECIDED (2026-06-19): NO backfill. The field defaults to True, so historical snapshots/DB load as exit_enabled=true (their exact historical behavior); a blanket rewrite would only churn config hashes. An audit (Task 7) documents the implicit-true history; only the buy-and-hold profile sets the key explicitly (to false). (superseded: the earlier full-100%-backfill decision)

    • [ ] Step 3: Create the model (mirror always_none, emit LONG)

    Create modules/model-trainer/src/rainbow/model_trainer/models/always_long.py:

    """Buy-and-hold baseline model: always predicts LONG (never NONE, never SHORT).

Non-trainable baseline. Mirrors TradingAlwaysNoneModel but targets the LONG class (index 1).
Combined with a bot profile that disables SL/TP/uncertainty/halt exits, a single LONG entry is
held to the end of the session, producing a constrained buy-and-hold equity curve with the full
investor metric suite.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch
from torch import nn

from rainbow.model_trainer.models.base import BaseModel

# Class index contract (matches BaseModel output): 0=NONE, 1=LONG, 2=SHORT.
_LONG_CLASS_INDEX = 1


class TradingAlwaysLongModel(BaseModel):
    """Always emits LONG with a fixed logit margin. Auxiliary outputs are fixed constants."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        input_dim: int,
        seq_len: int,
        num_classes: int,
        strength_value: float,
        quality_value: float,
        sampled_logit_margin: float,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.seq_len = seq_len
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.strength_value = strength_value
        self.quality_value = quality_value
        self.sampled_logit_margin = sampled_logit_margin
        # Differentiable anchor so the (non-trainable) model is still loop-compatible.
        self._anchor = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        batch_size = x.shape[0]
        logits = torch.zeros(batch_size, self.num_classes, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        logits[:, _LONG_CLASS_INDEX] = self.sampled_logit_margin + (self._anchor.sum() * 0.0)
        strength = torch.full((batch_size, 1), self.strength_value, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        quality = torch.full((batch_size, 1), self.quality_value, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        return {"logits": logits, "strength": strength, "quality": quality}

    Task 7: Audit the implicit exit_enabled=true history (no backfill)

    Status: DONE (2026-06-20) — audit at docs/audit/20260620_EXIT_ENABLED_DEFAULT_AUDIT.md (measured scope: ~6,809 on-disk JSON snapshots and 972 experiment / 9,746 session DB config rows embed stop_loss_config; only the always_long baseline sets exit_enabled explicitly — the rest load as true).

    Decision (D6, 2026-06-19): no backfill. Adding exit_enabled with a True default changes no behavior — every historical snapshot and DB config that lacks the key loads as exit_enabled=true, exactly what those runs did. Rewriting the ~6,797 JSON snapshots and the two DB config columns would only churn config hashes for zero behavioral gain (the same lesson as the trailing-stop remediation). Instead of a migration, this task records the fact in an audit.

    Files:

    • Create: docs/audit/<date>_EXIT_ENABLED_DEFAULT_AUDIT.md

    • [ ] Step 1: Write the audit documenting:

    • exit_enabled defaults to True on StopLossConfig / TakeProfitConfig.
    • All historical configs (snapshots under data/ and the DB columns experiments.experiment_config_json / backtest_sessions.bot_config_json) lack the key and therefore load as exit_enabled=true — i.e. they always closed on SL/TP, which matches their recorded behavior. No backfill is performed; the configs stay intentionally implicit.
    • The config hash computed now (with the field) differs from a historical stored hash (without it); this is expected and benign — the same old-vs-new hash divergence already documented for the trailing stop — and the strategy behavior is unchanged.

    • The only config that sets the key explicitly is the buy-and-hold profile (exit_enabled: false).

    • [ ] Step 2: Commit

    git add docs/audit/<date>_EXIT_ENABLED_DEFAULT_AUDIT.md
git commit -m "docs(audit): exit_enabled defaults to true; historical configs implicitly enabled (no backfill)"

    4. Cross-Fold Reporting Integration (handoff, not new work here)

    The buy-and-hold baseline is a normal backtest session/trial, so it flows through the cross-fold and investor-summary reporting defined in docs/plans/THESIS-SCRIPT2/_archived/20260601_SCRIPT2_CROSS_FOLD_REPORTING_AND_INVESTOR_METRICS_PLAN.md. The only reporting decision is its cross-fold identity label (recommend a dedicated always_long baseline identity so it is never pooled with the rule_based TA baseline). No reporting code is written in this plan; this is a handoff note so the cross-fold plan accounts for the new baseline.

    5. Out of Scope

    • Short-side sell_and_hold (D5).
    • A "none" stop-loss TYPE (we keep SL computed; only the exit action is gated).
    • Changing the synthetic Benchmark RC computation (it remains the cheap per-run scalar reference; the executed buy-and-hold is the full-metric comparison surface and is expected to diverge from the synthetic figure because of entry latency, commission, and slippage).
    • Any backtest-engine loop change (none required).
